# Quick Facts - The Great North American Total Solar Eclipse of April 8th 2024
**The 2024 Great North American Solar Eclipse will be the most viewed eclipse in human history.** There will be huge media attention; Weather on April 8 th is predicted to be generally fair (although clouds can occur anywhere); There are large populations in
cities located on and near the eclipse path; There is ease of access to observe the total eclipse due to the extensive highway system in USA; Everyone in the continental USA will see at least a partial eclipse.

...

**The eclipse path crosses 15 states across** some of the most densely populated areas of the USA.
Those states include Texas; Oklahoma; Arkansas; Missouri; Tennessee; Kentucky; Illinois; Indiana; Ohio; Michigan; Pennsylvania; New York; Vermont; New Hampshire; Maine.

...

## WATCH LIVE: Solar eclipse 2024
The line of totality — or where there will be complete sun coverage — will span 15 states, but a partial eclipse will appear in all continental U.S. states, according to NASA.
The eclipse route will travel from Mexico, arching northeast from Texas to Ohio before reaching Canada and going back into Maine.

excerpts:
# When is the next total solar eclipse?
After that, the next total solar eclipse will occur on March 30, 2033, but totality will be visible only from Alaska and Russia.
On Aug. 23, 2044, an eclipse’s path of totality will pass over some of the U.S.: Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, parts of Canada and Greenland.
Then, finally, on Aug. 12, 2045, a total solar eclipse will once again trace a path from coast to coast across the continental U.S., similar to the one this year.

# What to know about the August 2026 total solar eclipse and where you can see it in the US
## Who can see the total solar eclipse?
### Where can you see the eclipse in the U.S.?
Many locations in the Northern Hemisphere will experience a partial solar eclipse, including parts of the northern United States, from Alaska to North Carolina.

...

## Popular Reads
### When was the last total solar eclipse visible in the U.S.?
The last total solar eclipse visible from the United States occurred on April 8, 2024, when the path of totality crossed 15 states from Texas to Maine, according to [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/eclipses/future-eclipses/eclipse-2024/where-when/?) .
[Related 105-year-old Texas man prepares for his 13th total solar eclipse on April 8](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/105-year-texas-man-prepares-13th-total-solar-108968089)
[](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/105-year-texas-man-prepares-13th-total-solar-108968089)

### When is the next total solar eclipse in the U.S.?
The next total solar eclipse visible from any part of the United States will occur on March 30, 2033, when totality will be visible only in Alaska, [NASA](https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5212/) says.
The next total solar eclipse visible from the contiguous United States is expected on Aug. 23, 2044. Another coast-to-coast total solar eclipse will follow on Aug. 12, 2045.

excerpts:
# Total solar eclipse dazzles observers on August 12, 2026
## August 12, 2026, total solar eclipse
The second solar eclipse of 2026 will be a total solar eclipse on Wednesday, August 12, 2026. The total solar eclipse will sweep across the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, and Spain. And it’ll be visible as a partial eclipse from much of western Europe and North America.

...

### Path of totality
The eclipse path lasted over 92 minutes and covered 5,157 miles (8,300 kilometers) – or just 0.47% – of the Earth.
Remember to [convert UTC](https://earthsky.org/astronomy-essentials/universal-time/) to your time. Note the different between UTC and [UT1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Time) .

...

### Next eclipse and eclipse seasons
Bottom line: On August 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse will be visible parts of Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, and Spain. And it’ll be visible as a partial eclipse from much of western Europe and North America.
